uses.label: Chlorophyll and cyanobacteria
uses.definition: Chlorophyll absorbs red light near 665 nm and fluoresces near 680 nm, and dense blooms reflect a peak near 710 nm. Cyanobacteria add phycocyanin absorption near 620 nm.
uses.quote: For low biomass, oligotrophic to mesotrophic waterbodies, the chl-a spectrum is characterized by a sun-induced fluorescence peak around 680 nm [84–86]. For high biomass, eutrophic waterbodies, the florescence signal is masked by absorption features and backscatter peaks centered at 665 nm and 710 nm respectively [87]. The ratio between these two wavelengths has been used to accurately estimate chl-a concentrations in numerous studies [88–90].
uses.locator: Section 2.1 Chlorophyll-A

uses.label: Turbidity and suspended sediment
uses.definition: Suspended particles raise reflectance and move the reflectance maximum from green toward red and near-infrared wavelengths. Single red or near-infrared bands track suspended sediment.
uses.quote: As inorganic TSS concentrations increase within a waterbody, the location of the spectral maximum moves from around 550 nm into the red or near-infrared wavelengths [49] with waterbody specific variation dependent on chlorophyll and CDOM concentrations.
uses.locator: Section 2.2 Total Suspended Solids

uses.label: Dissolved organic matter
uses.definition: Colored dissolved organic matter, also called yellow matter, absorbs blue and green light. Absorption rises exponentially toward shorter wavelengths, so retrievals ratio red against green or blue.
uses.quote: The increase in the CDOM concentration mainly affects the reflectance values in the blue and green region of the spectrum (especially below ~500 nm) and its absorbance increases exponentially with decreasing wavelength.
uses.locator: Section 4.2 Colored Dissolved Organic Matters (CDOM)

uses.label: Surface temperature
uses.definition: Thermal infrared bands measure emitted radiant heat, which gives the radiant temperature of the water surface. Clouds block the measurement.
uses.quote: Thermal infrared bands are able to measure the amount of infrared radiant heat emitted from land surfaces and the radiant temperature of waterbodies that have environmental and economic import.
uses.locator: Section 4.6 Water Temperature

uses.label: Atmospheric correction and screening
uses.definition: Aerosol, water vapor, cirrus, cloud, and sun glint add signal that a water retrieval must remove or mask. Absorption bands and near and shortwave infrared bands estimate these terms.
uses.quote: Monitoring of water quality by satellite ocean colour data requires high quality atmospheric correction and especially the accurate quantification of the aerosol contribution to the top of atmosphere radiance.
uses.locator: Abstract

uses.label: Water extent and shoreline
uses.definition: Water absorbs near-infrared and shortwave infrared light and appears dark where land is bright. Green to infrared indices such as NDWI and MNDWI separate water from land.
uses.quote: In the Near-IR and Mid-IR regions, water increasingly absorbs the light and makes it look darker, which varies based on water depth and wavelength.
uses.locator: Section 4.4 Turbidity and Total Suspended Sediments

sensors.quote: An Ocean and Land Colour Instrument (OLCI), based on ENVISAT's Medium Resolution Imaging Spectrometer (MERIS). With 21 bands, compared to 15 bands on MERIS, a design optimised to minimise sun-glint and a resolution of 300 m over all surfaces, OLCI marks a new generation of measurements over the ocean and land.

sensors.label: Sentinel-3 SLSTR
sensors.instrument: Sea and Land Surface Temperature Radiometer (SLSTR)
notes: S1 to S6 sample at 500 m. S7 to S9, F1, and F2 sample at 1 km. The Resolution column of Table 2 spans those rows.
Centers, widths, and functions come from Table 2 of the SLSTR Products page. The page gives no band names, so the name field carries the Comments group cell.
The instrument page names S4 (1.375 µm) and S6 (2.25 µm) as new channels for improved cloud detection.
S7, S8, and S9 retrieve sea and land surface temperature. F1 and F2 share detectors with S7 and S8 and add dynamic range for fires.
The Function column holds two typos, '>Cloud screening' and 'loud clearing'. Quotes keep them verbatim.
sensors.quote: SLSTR measures in nine spectral channels and two additional bands. A 1.3 micron band aimed at cirrus detection and a 2 micron band aimed at vegetation, mineral and atmospheric corrections for very turbid waters. An SLSTR with spatial resolution in the visible and shortwave infra-red channels of 500 m and 1 km in the thermal infra-red channels.

uses.quote: For low biomass, oligotrophic to mesotrophic waterbodies, the chl-a spectrum is characterized by a sun-induced fluorescence peak around 680 nm [84–86]. For high biomass, eutrophic waterbodies, the florescence signal is masked by absorption features and backscatter peaks centered at 665 nm and 710 nm respectively [87]. limitations: MDPI pages return HTTP 403 to this environment. Gholizadeh et al. 2016 is cited from its PubMed Central copy. Topp et al. 2020 is cited from the Carolina Digital Repository PDF.
Toming et al. 2016 is not cited. Its MDPI page was unreachable and no open copy was found. Soomets et al. 2020 in PubMed Central supplies the Sentinel-2 wavelengths instead.
ScienceDirect and Optica pages block automated access. Vanhellemont and Ruddick 2015 and Vanhellemont 2023 are cited from open PDF copies in the VLIZ repository.

Taylor and Francis pages block automated access. Wynne et al. 2008, Nechad et al. 2010, McFeeters 1996, and Xu 2006 are not cited. The USGS DSWE algorithm document and the SentiWiki NDWI entry stand in.
The SentiWiki S2 Mission page lists bands by number without names. Names come from the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem S2L2A and S2L1C pages.
The Data Space pages list centers that differ from SentiWiki by up to 0.4 nm for some bands, for example B02 492.4 versus 492.7 nm. The record uses SentiWiki.
The S3 OLCI Instrument page lists Oa09 at 673.25 nm and Oa16 at 778.85 nm. The OLCI Products page lists 673.75 nm and 778.75 nm. The record follows the products page.
The USGS Landsat 9 page and band FAQ name the instruments OLI and TIRS. The OLI-2 and TIRS-2 names come from NASA photo captions on the Landsat 9 science page.
TIRS bands 10 and 11 carry resolution_m 30 per the schema rule on product pixel size. Their acquired resolution is 100 m, recorded in the band note.
The MODIS specifications page gives no band names. The name field carries the Primary Use group label. A banner states that NASA is not updating the site during a lapse in federal funding.
Planet's PSScene product specification PDF sits behind a Widen viewer page with a signed, expiring download link. The cited URL is the viewer page. The PDF is dated June 2026.
Planet's PSB.SD table gives center and fwhm. Planet's range table and Vanhellemont 2023 give slightly different edges and centers. The record uses the center and fwhm table.
Wavelength-basis uses come from point wavelengths that a source ties to a use, plus one half-range, CDOM below about 500 nm. Broad single-band ranges from Gholizadeh's Table 8 were not applied.
Landsat 8 statements from Vanhellemont and Ruddick 2015 apply to Landsat 9 by wavelength, not by band number. USGS states that the Landsat 9 OLI is a copy of the Landsat 8 OLI.
For the USGS DSWE extent use, only green, NIR, SWIR1, and SWIR2 are marked. Blue and red also enter AWESH and MBSRV but stay unmarked to keep the column selective.
No source names Sentinel-2 B11 or B12, MODIS, OLCI, SLSTR, or PlanetScope bands for water extent. Those bands carry no extent use.
MODIS bands 24, 25, 30, and 33 to 36 carry no use. Their groups, Atmospheric Temperature, Ozone, and Cloud Top Altitude, sit outside the vocabulary or lack a water retrieval tie.
Per-satellite values exist for Sentinel-2 only. The OLCI, SLSTR, MODIS, and Planet pages give one set of values for all platforms.
Only the USGS FAQs (Updated Date: August 10, 2026) and the NASA Landsat 9 page (Page Last Updated Sep 17, 2026) display an update date. Other pages carry null.
Table cells that break lines are quoted with a single space at the break. Examples are the OLCI Oa08 function and the MODIS ocean color group.
The Gholizadeh review names the TIR band of OLI/TIRS without a band number. Both TIRS bands carry the temperature use on that basis.
The Landsat 9 panchromatic band spans 500 to 680 nm and contains several anchors. It is excluded from wavelength-basis uses because it merges green to red light.
OLCI and SLSTR pages give no band names. OLCI names carry the Function cell verbatim. SLSTR names carry the Comments group cell, VNIR, SWIR, or the thermal group.
